newsitem.title: SPAIN: Slain politician's hometown determined to defy ETA.
newsitem.headline: Slain politician's hometown determined to defy ETA.

text.p: The hometown of a politician slain by Basque separatists is determined to lash back at the rebels who once intimidated them, emboldened by support from millions of Spaniards who protested at his killing.

One week after 29-year-old Miguel Angel Blanco's abduction, the grieving village of Ermua where he lived and served as a town councillor has come to symbolise a new spirit of defiance in the Basque country and throughout Spain.
"In Ermua, there used to be much fear of talking about politics, about the terrorists. We are not afraid anymore," said Evagelina Simon, an acquaintance of Blanco's family.
The killing marked a sea change in Spanish public opinion, sending an estimated six million people into the streets to declare they had had enough of the guerrilla group ETA.
"We have the support of all of Spain. For us that is very important," said Maria Luisa Gonzalez, a nurse from Ermua.
Blanco was kidnapped on July 10 and ETA threatened to kill him 48 hours later if Spain did not meet its demand for a prisoner transfer. The government refused and Blanco was shot twice in the head.

Spaniards were incensed that the guerrillas had targeted someone with whom many could so easily identify -- an ordinary functionary who was a low-ranking member of Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar's Popular Party.
"We have to go village by village in the Basque region to liberate the people from the shadow of ETA," Ermua Mayor Carlos Totorica said in a television interview on Thursday.
"The freedom of expression or to act out politically, the right to live freely did not exist...I think that this has changed significantly in the Basque region. In Ermua it has."
The government vowed a crackdown on the rebels and their political arm Herri Batasuna.

On Thursday, an explosion in an apartment in the Basque town of Durango led to the discovery of an ETA hideout packed with grenades and launchers ready for firing along with bomb parts, detonators and chemicals.
Authorities were searching for at least three suspects who fled the hideout after a grenade apparently went off by accident, officials said.

The Basque government said investigators found no connection between the residents of the "safe house" and Blanco's killing. Spanish state radio reported, however, that at least two of the fugitives had been under scrutiny for possible links to it.

In Ermua, a bleak working class Basque town of 17,000 people, a burnt shell of an office used by ETA's political wing Herri Batasuna is testimony to the groundswell of sentiment against the group spreading across the troubled Basque region.
"The better known Herri Batasuna people would run a physical risk in Ermua at this time without a doubt," the mayor said. "Many of them have left. The village is very angry."
One Herri Batasuna supporter said she had received death threats by phone the day Blanco was killed.

"War has been declared against Herri Batasuna and its voters...We are afraid," said the woman who asked not to be named. "Now those of us who vote HB we can't live in Ermua. Those who have businesses, we can die of hunger."
Outside Blanco's family home, a dozen bouquets of flowers and notes of sympathy decorate the entrance way. One poster calls for a boycott of all Herri Batasuna-owned businesses.
There have been scattered attacks on Herri Batasuna supporters and offices since the killing, stoking fears of a more widespread civilian conflict in the region.
Basque political leaders and the central government in Madrid have vowed to isolate Herri Batasuna, a political party with nearly 15 percent support in the region.

The Basque government has barred the group from holding a demonstration on Saturday for fear it would unleash sectarian violence. Herri Batasuna said it had appealed against the decision in court and would abide by the ruling if they upheld the order.
"We don't want it to end in a massacre," Herri Batasuna leader Floren Aoiz told reporters on Thursday.
